name: Weekly Cisplatin Radiosensitizer (concurrent chemoradiation)
cyclesNote: single-agent cisplatin given weekly as a radiosensitizer during external-beam pelvic radiation, typically 5 to 6 weekly doses spanning the radiation course

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

premedications.name: Cisplatin hydration and antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.notes: pre- and post-cisplatin IV hydration with attention to urine output; give antiemetic prophylaxis before each weekly dose (cisplatin is a highly emetogenic agent even at the weekly radiosensitizing dose).

supportiveCare: IV hydration with each weekly cisplatin dose to protect renal function.
Antiemetics before each dose per emetic-risk framework.
Coordinate each dose to fall on a radiation treatment day for radiosensitization.
monitoring: renal function (creatinine/GFR) and magnesium before each weekly dose
audiometry / neuropathy assessment as clinically indicated

doseModificationRules.condition: creatinine clearance reduced or rising creatinine
doseModificationRules.text: Hold or reduce cisplatin for declining renal function; the physician decides on a per-dose basis.

drugs.name: Cisplatin
drugs.notes: Cisplatin 40 mg/m2 IV once weekly as a single-agent radiosensitizer given concurrently with external-beam pelvic radiation, commonly 5 to 6 weekly doses over the radiation course. A conventional per-dose cap of about 70 mg is applied to the weekly radiosensitizing dose. Standard Guidelines / DeVita / Harrison, general reference. DRAFT, experimental.
